entities.summary: Gennaro Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte was a prominent Italian Cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church and a key figure in the Vatican during World War II. He played a crucial role in the Allied victory and was instrumental in the post-war reorganization of the Catholic Church. Born into a noble family, Granito was educated at the Pontifical Gregorian University and later served as the Apostolic Nuncio to the United Kingdom. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure the release of Allied prisoners of war and facilitated the rebuilding of relationships between the Catholic Church and the British government. Granito's legacy extends beyond his official duties, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of social justice causes. He died on February 16, 1948, leaving behind a legacy of faith, diplomacy, and service to the greater good.
